references.text: Samson was bound with bronze chains, which recalls how prisoners of war were often treated in the Old Testament
King Zedekiah had his eyes put out by the Babylonians, the same fate that befell Samson when the Philistines blinded him
Zedekiah was blinded and bound with bronze chains, a parallel to Samson's fate of blindness and chains
Samson had gone to Gaza before, and now he is taken back there as a prisoner—an ironic twist in the story
Even though Samson was blinded and imprisoned, he finally took his revenge on the Philistines
Grinding grain by hand mill was usually work for slaves and prisoners, which Samson was now forced to do
Young men carried millstones as heavy slave labor, similar to the work Samson was assigned in prison
